archetype.name: Pocket Passer (big-arm)
archetype.definition: A tall, strong-armed thrower who has produced top-15-caliber EPA in most seasons from the pocket, and who has added real scramble value lately but wins first with his arm.

report.headline: A proven passer buried by a collapsed line, missing receivers and his own deep misses
report.take:
Herbert's track record is not in question. In four of his six previous seasons he finished top 16 in EPA per play, including 0.167 in 2024 and 0.09 last year on an 11-5 team. This season he sits 38th of 43 at -0.193 per dropback, 0-5, with 7 interceptions and a 10.6% sack rate. A drop that sharp from a quarterback that established needs a cause, and the dossier shows several.

The biggest is the protection. The Chargers rank last in the league in rate of QB hits allowed, he has been hit or sacked on 22.6% of dropbacks, and the injury list is the offensive line: Rashawn Slater and Trevor Penning on IR, Joe Alt and Kayode Awosika out. Under Harbaugh the offense also passes 12.1 points less often than the situation predicts, the lowest rate in the league, so he sees lots of obvious passing downs. His third-down plays come with 8.6 yards to go on average and produce -0.316 EPA. The receiver room is falling apart too. Quentin Johnston is out, Tre' Harris is doubtful, and Ladd McConkey is questionable after being active but playing zero snaps in Week 5. McConkey has been his best target by far at 0.629 EPA per target.

Not all of it is circumstance. His pressure-to-sack rate has climbed for years, from 17.1% as a rookie to 33.3% in 2024 and 29.7% last season, so the habit of holding the ball predates this line. His bad-throw rate of 15.4% is worse than the 13.3% of the last two seasons. The real damage is downfield. On 57 throws of 10+ air yards he has 7 interceptions and 1 touchdown, while his passes behind the line and under 10 yards are positive. The numbers also aren't inflated by garbage time; the close games are where it breaks. He is at -0.345 within one score and -1.155 in close fourth quarters, taking 9 sacks on 28 plays there. Trailing by 9+ he is near neutral at -0.029.

The red zone is the one area that still works, at 78.6% completions, 5 TDs and no interceptions. That suggests the processing is intact when the field is compressed and the protection only has to hold briefly. Turning this around depends on bodies returning, not on any change in him. Alt and the receivers are listed with October 18 return estimates, but Alt and Johnston are already ruled out for this week. Slater and Penning are estimated around mid-November.

strengths.title: Clean in the red zone
strengths.body: All five of his touchdown passes came in the red zone, on 78.6% completions, 0 interceptions and a +21.5 CPOE. Short fields shrink the protection problem and the need to push the ball downfield. The completion rate over expected will cool on 14 attempts, but the no-turnover efficiency fits a passer with his history.

strengths.title: Short game still functions
strengths.body: Throws under 10 air yards are at +0.149 EPA with a 50% success rate and no interceptions. Screens and passes behind the line are also positive. This is the plan that survives a broken line, and it should stay usable as long as the running back and slot targets are available.

strengths.title: A long baseline of competence
strengths.body: He has posted positive EPA per play every season of his career, peaking at 0.199 in 2021, and he ran for 498 yards last year. A five-game sample behind a decimated roster does not erase six years of evidence. It is the strongest reason to expect recovery once the personnel returns.

concerns.title: Turnovers on every downfield throw
concerns.body: On 18 deep attempts he has completed 27.8% with 3 interceptions. On 39 intermediate throws he has 4 more. Some of that comes from throwing under pressure without his top receivers, but his career interception ranks are often near the bottom (58th, 55th and 60th in three of the last five seasons). The tendency is part of who he is and has been amplified this year.

concerns.title: Line collapse and sack habit
concerns.body: The Chargers are last in QB hits allowed and have four linemen out or on IR. His pressure-to-sack rate was already 29.7% last year, so a line this compromised turns pressure into drive-killing sacks, 14 of them in one-score games. This improves when Alt returns, but it will not be fixed before Slater and Penning come back around mid-November.

concerns.title: Accuracy has slipped too
concerns.body: His -4.81 CPOE and 15.4% bad-throw rate are both worse than his recent seasons, and the no-huddle has been ugly at -26.8 CPOE on 14 attempts. Throwing to backups under pressure explains part of it. A run of bad-throw games from 18.5% to 23.3% still means mechanics under duress are worth watching.

trend.note: His per-game pass EPA has worsened in each of the last three games, from -6.4 to -8.0 to -10.3. Week 5 was the low point: 121 yards and 5 sacks against Denver, a game McConkey sat out after being active.

nextGame.headline: Weak Chiefs pass rush helps, but the supporting cast is gone
nextGame.body:
Kansas City's defense brings one real gift: it barely gets home. The Chiefs rank 31st in sack rate at 2.5% and 22nd in QB-hit rate. That is the best possible opponent for a line missing four linemen and a quarterback whose problems start with pressure. Everything else points the other way. The Chiefs allow only 12.4 PPR a game to quarterbacks (3rd), one TD a game (2nd), and rank 6th against explosive passes and short passes. Herbert's short-game escape hatch runs straight into a strength of theirs. They have also been the stingiest defense in the league against WR1s on a per-play basis. Their soft spots are tight ends and WR3s, and tight ends draw 32.9% of the targets against them.

Availability decides this. Alt and Johnston are out, Harris is doubtful and McConkey is questionable after sitting out Week 5, so Herbert could be throwing to a mostly backup receiver group on the road, as an 8.5-point underdog, in a division game. The forecast is still early, but 16 mph sustained wind with 27 mph gusts would further limit a deep game that is already his worst area. On the Kansas City side, Rashee Rice is questionable but trending toward playing after the bye. The Chiefs' offense ranks 4th in EPA, so the Chargers' 6th-ranked defense will have to keep it close.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers' battered line vs. a quiet rush
keyMatchups.body: Kansas City's 2.5% sack rate is the league's second-lowest. That gives Herbert a rare week where his 10.6% sack rate should come down even without Alt. If he can't stay upright against this front, the protection problem is worse than injuries alone.

keyMatchups.title: Tight-end funnel for Gadsden
keyMatchups.body: Defenses send tight ends 32.9% of targets against the Chiefs, against a league share of 23.8%, and the top tight end scores 3.2 PPR over his average. With the WR room depleted, Oronde Gadsden II should see volume. His -0.484 EPA per target so far tempers how much that helps.

keyMatchups.title: Short game meets a short-game defense
keyMatchups.body: His underneath passing has been his most efficient area. The Chiefs rank 6th in short-pass EPA allowed and 6th in explosive pass rate, so the easy completions shrink. That points to long, patient drives that rarely finish.

nextGame.watch: Whether McConkey plays. He has been Herbert's only consistently efficient wideout, and without him the offense is down to Mitchell and the tight end underneath.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect slow, uneven improvement rather than a quick snap-back. Alt and the receivers carry October 18 return estimates, though Alt and Johnston are already out for this week. If they return on that schedule, the sack rate and the receiver-dependent efficiency should recover first. A 7-interception pace on 143 attempts is higher than even his turnover-prone seasons and should come down, as should a sack rate inflated by four missing linemen. Harbaugh's run-heavy approach caps his volume, so a 2021-style yardage season is off the table.

The red-zone perfection will regress, and so will the bottom-five accuracy numbers, given his career CPOE was positive in three of the last four years. By the time Slater returns around mid-November he should look like a league-average-plus starter again. The near term, with backup receivers and a patched line, looks closer to what we've seen.
swingFactors: Return dates for Alt, Slater and Penning
Whether the deep-ball interceptions keep coming

bets.reason: He just threw for 121 yards, his top three wideouts are out, doubtful or questionable, and Kansas City ranks 6th in short-pass EPA and explosive pass rate allowed. The early wind forecast and a run-heavy offense (last in pass rate over expected) push the same way.

He has thrown at least one interception in all five games, 7 in total, mostly on intermediate and deep throws. As an 8.5-point road underdog with backup receivers, he will likely be pushing the ball late.

Four of five Chargers games have gone under, the offense ranks last in EPA and has scored no more than 23 points, and their defense ranks 6th. Kansas City's 4th-ranked offense is the risk, and the wind forecast is early but leans the same way.
The obvious read after 17 sacks behind a gutted line is more of the same. Kansas City's pass rush ranks 31st in sack rate at 2.5% and 22nd in hit rate, the weakest he has faced.

confidence.note: Five-game sample, offensive injuries changing week to week, but a long career baseline to lean on.
